s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic heel pain with limited response to treatment
salient_findings: Tight gastrocnemius muscle with positive Silfverskiöld test
Pedunculated bony protrusion on the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus
key_facts: 41-year-old man with long-standing left plantar heel pain
Symptoms persisted for over two and a half years
Previous treatments included physiotherapy, anti-inflammatory and analgesic medications, and two surgical releases
Temporary relief from previous treatments
Recurrent heel pain upon return to work
Antalgic gait
Tight gastrocnemius muscle
Non-specific tenderness over the plantar aspect of the calcaneus
Normal bony relationships on weight-bearing radiographs
No fractures, lesions, or signs of arthritis on radiographs
No thickening of the plantar fascia on MRI
No signal alteration in adjacent soft tissues or bone marrow on MRI
Presence of a pedunculated bony protrusion on the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus on MRI

shortlist.label: Haglund's deformity
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a pedunculated bony protrusion on the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus on MRI

shortlist.label: Baxter's nerve entrapment
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic heel pain with limited response to treatment and presence of a bony protrusion

shortlist.label: Osteoid osteoma of the calcaneus
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent heel pain and presence of a bony protrusion on MRI

shortlist.label: Calcaneal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a bony protrusion on MRI and chronic heel pain

shortlist.label: Gastrocnemius tightness
shortlist.why_kept: Tight gastrocnemius muscle and positive Silfverskiöld test

raw.rationale: The presence of a pedunculated bony protrusion on the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus on MRI, which is consistent with the characteristics of an osteoid osteoma, a benign bone tumor that can cause persistent pain.

rejected.label: Haglund's deformity
rejected.why: Haglund's deformity typically presents with a bony prominence at the posterior superior aspect of the calcaneus, which does not match the location of the bony protrusion in this case.

rejected.label: Baxter's nerve entrapment
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence of nerve entrapment or neuropathic symptoms in the case presentation.

rejected.label: Calcaneal bone cyst
rejected.why: The MRI findings do not indicate a cystic lesion, but rather a bony protrusion, which is not consistent with a bone cyst.

rejected.label: Gastrocnemius tightness
rejected.why: While the patient has a tight gastrocnemius muscle, this alone does not explain the persistent heel pain and the presence of a bony protrusion on MRI.
